Aerospace NDT training in Savannah: the short answer

Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based aerospace NDT training to Savannah employers and technicians. The theory runs live online and the practical work runs onsite at your own facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Courses cover penetrant (PT), eddy current (ET), ultrasonic (UT, including composite and bond-line work), radiography (RT) and visual testing (VT) at Levels I and II, plus Level III exam preparation. We are not a NAS 410 certifying body. If your employer certifies under NAS 410, our training feeds into its written practice. It does not replace it.

That last point matters more in Savannah than in most cities. Business-jet manufacturing, completions and heavy maintenance at Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport dominate the local aerospace economy, and most of that work runs under NAS 410 written practices, OEM flow-downs and Nadcap audits. So the first question for anyone looking for aerospace NDT training in Savannah isn't where the nearest classroom is. It's which written practice will certify you, and what that document accepts as formal training. This page answers that question honestly for the employers, suppliers and technicians around Chatham, Effingham and Bryan counties, and shows where Atlantis fits and where it doesn't.

Atlantis has no training centre in Savannah or anywhere else. Theory is taught live online, so a technician in Pooler, Port Wentworth, Richmond Hill or Rincon can join from home or a shop office. Practical sessions happen onsite at the employer's facility, on the employer's own penetrant line, eddy current instruments, UT flaw detectors and reference standards. For aerospace work that's usually the better model anyway, because your practical exam has to be on the part families and procedures your technicians will actually sign off.

Aerospace NDT work in Savannah

Savannah's aerospace NDT market has three layers. Each one asks for slightly different things from an inspector.

  • Business-jet manufacturing and completions. Gulfstream Aerospace is headquartered at the airport and builds, completes and flight-tests large-cabin business jets there. Production inspection means fluorescent penetrant on machined and formed aluminium and titanium details, eddy current on fastener holes and conductivity checks, ultrasonic examination of bonded and composite structure, and radiography of castings and assemblies where the drawing calls for it. Production NDT is procedure-driven. The inspector follows a written technique against a specification, and a Level 3 owns the technique.
  • Heavy maintenance and MRO. Gulfstream's customer-support operation in Savannah is one of the largest business-aviation service footprints in the country. The Savannah Service Center East expansion opened in 2024 and added hangar and back-shop space. Maintenance NDT is a different discipline from production NDT. Technicians work from the aircraft manufacturer's NDT manual and structural repair data, inspect in-service aircraft for fatigue cracking and corrosion, and work in hangar conditions rather than on a line. Eddy current (surface, bolt-hole and low-frequency) and ultrasonic thickness and bond testing carry more of the load here.
  • The supplier and military tail. Machine shops, sheet-metal fabricators, composite repair shops, plating and heat-treat processors and component overhaul shops around the airport, Pooler and the I-95 and I-16 corridors supply both the OEM and the MRO side. Many carry their own NDT capability or buy it from Nadcap-accredited labs. Military aviation is also present: Army aviation at Hunter Army Airfield and the Air National Guard flying mission at the airport both run their own NDI under military technical orders, separate from civilian certification.

The practical result is that a Savannah aerospace NDT technician is usually certified under an employer's NAS 410 written practice when working for the OEM or a Nadcap-accredited supplier, and under a Part 145 repair station's training programme (often referencing NAS 410 or the FAA's advisory material on NDI personnel) when working in MRO. SNT-TC-1A certification is common in the region's non-aerospace NDT work, such as port cranes, LNG and paper-mill piping and structural steel, and among smaller suppliers whose customers accept it. See our general NDT training page for Savannah for that side of the market.

Aerospace NDT methods for Savannah work, and the specifications behind them

The table maps each method to the kind of Savannah aerospace work it typically supports and the specifications that usually govern it. Your customer's purchase order, the OEM's process specification and your written practice always take precedence over this general list.

MethodAerospace application in SavannahTypical code / standard
Penetrant testing (PT), fluorescentProduction inspection of machined and formed aluminium, titanium and stainless details; in-service crack checks during heavy maintenanceASTM E1417, AMS 2644 materials, OEM process specs
Eddy current testing (ET)Bolt-hole and fastener-site inspection, surface crack detection on aluminium structure, conductivity verification after heat treatment, corrosion checks in MROOEM NDT manual procedures, SAE ARP4402 (open fastener holes), ASTM E1004 (conductivity)
Ultrasonic testing (UT)Bond-line and laminate inspection of composite and bonded structure, thickness checks for corrosion, forging and plate inspection at suppliersASTM E2375 (wrought products), OEM composite and bond specs, NDT manual procedures
Phased array UT (PAUT)Faster coverage of composite panels and bonded assemblies where the OEM has qualified the techniqueOEM-qualified techniques under the employer's written practice
Radiographic testing (RT) / digital radiographyCastings, complex assemblies, water ingress in honeycomb structure, specified weld jointsASTM E1742, ASTM E2033 / E2698 for digital techniques where specified
Magnetic particle testing (MT)Steel landing-gear and actuator components, fittings and fasteners at overhaul shopsASTM E1444, OEM specs
Visual testing (VT)The baseline for every inspection; borescope work on engines and structure during maintenanceOEM maintenance data, employer procedures

Savannah method spotlight: eddy current for business-jet MRO. If a Savannah technician asks us which second method to add, the honest answer for the MRO side is usually ET. Business jets fly long service lives with repeated inspection intervals, and the manufacturer's NDT manual calls up a large number of eddy current tasks: bolt-hole inspection at fastener rows, surface probes on fittings and skins, and low-frequency techniques for second-layer cracking and corrosion. A technician with PT Level II who adds ET becomes far more useful on a hangar floor. Our ET course covers impedance-plane interpretation, probe and frequency selection, reference standards, and the documentation habits an aerospace auditor will check. The practical sessions run on your instruments and standards. See eddy current testing in aviation and our ET Level II course.

Which certification scheme Savannah aerospace employers expect

This is the question most aerospace training pages skip. The table lays out the schemes you'll meet in Savannah, who asks for each, and how SNT-TC-1A-based training from Atlantis fits. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only. The other schemes are listed so you know what your employer may require, not because we offer them.

SchemeWho requires it in SavannahDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?

The theory content overlaps heavily, and some NAS 410 written practices accept external formal training once their Responsible Level 3 has reviewed the course content and hours. Certification is still issued by the employer under its NAS 410 written practice, including its own exams. Ask your Responsible Level 3 before you enrol.

We supply detailed records for that reason.

For a fuller comparison of the two main US documents, read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A. The practical takeaway for a Savannah technician: if you already work for, or are about to join, a NAS 410 employer, its Responsible Level 3 owns your certification path. The most useful thing an outside course can do is give you strong theory, method fluency and practice before that employer's exams. If you work for an SNT-TC-1A employer or plan to move into one, our courses map directly onto the written-practice route below.

The SNT-TC-1A certification path, step by step

Where your employer certifies under SNT-TC-1A, the route looks like this. The recommended minimum training and experience for each method and level are in our NDT training requirements matrix. Your employer's written practice may set more, and aerospace customers often expect more than the minimum.

  1. Confirm the governing written practice. Find out which document will certify you and whether the employer's customers impose aerospace-specific requirements on top. If the company has no written practice yet, that's the first gap to close (see employer services below).
  2. Complete formal classroom training in the method and level you're seeking, and keep the outline, hours, dates and instructor details. For Savannah crews, theory runs live online.
  3. Log documented on-the-job experience under certified personnel, method by method, with dates and hours, verified as you go. Aerospace auditors look closely at experience records, and reconstructing them later rarely survives scrutiny.
  4. Pass the general examination on the principles of the method, set and graded under a Level III's authority.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the employer's equipment, procedures, specifications and acceptance criteria. For aerospace work that means the actual OEM process specifications you'll apply.
  6. Pass the practical examination on real specimens with real discontinuities, such as cracked fastener-hole standards, penetrant panels and bonded test pieces, demonstrating set-up, detection, evaluation and reporting.
  7. Pass the vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation, with near vision repeated at least annually.
  8. Receive employer certification in writing for the method and level. It's valid with that employer.
  9. Maintain and recertify at the interval the written practice sets, keeping vision tests current and showing continuity in the method.

For the full background on how employer-based certification works, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiation licensing, airport access and security for Savannah aerospace NDT

Most aerospace radiography in Savannah uses X-ray rather than isotopes, often in shielded rooms or cabinets, but both are regulated. Georgia is an NRC Agreement State. Radioactive materials, including the gamma sources used for industrial radiography, are licensed and inspected by the Georgia Environmental Protection Division's Radioactive Materials Program. X-ray equipment is handled separately: non-medical and industrial X-ray users must register with the Georgia Department of Community Health before they operate, and the registration process includes a shielding design and an initial inspection. Radiation-safety training and radiographer qualification under these rules are legal requirements for the employer and the radiographer. They're separate from your NDT method certification, and an RT course from Atlantis doesn't replace them.

Access is the other practical constraint. Work airside at Savannah/Hilton Head International Airport needs airport security badging, which the employer sponsors. Work for military customers at Hunter Army Airfield or with the Air National Guard needs base-access credentials. Some defence-related programmes also restrict technical data under export-control rules, so the employer may require US-person status for certain work. Port-adjacent work around the Garden City terminals, which some Savannah NDT technicians also do, usually needs a TWIC card. None of these are training questions, but they decide who can be put on a job, so employers planning onsite sessions should allow for them.

Online, live-virtual and onsite delivery for Savannah aerospace crews

We deliver in three ways, and we'll tell you plainly which one suits your situation.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions in real time, not a video library, covering method physics, equipment, technique, specifications and interpretation. It works well for shift-based MRO crews because sessions can be scheduled around hangar shifts. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite practical sessions at your facility. We come to your shop or hangar and run the hands-on portion on your equipment, part families and reference standards, under ASNT Level III oversight. For aerospace this is the format that matters, because the specimens, procedures and acceptance criteria in the practical should match what your technicians will sign.
  • Employer cohorts. A group of technicians from one company, or from several suppliers who agree to train together, scheduled to fit aircraft induction dates and production rates. See corporate NDT training.

Scheduling is built around your workload, not a fixed public calendar. Tell us the methods, levels, headcount and the weeks you can release people, and we'll come back with a proposal. Request a Savannah aerospace training quote. We reply within one business day.

Employer services: written practices and Level III support for Savannah aerospace suppliers

A large share of the aerospace NDT work Atlantis does is for employers rather than individuals. Typical Savannah requests:

  • A supplier adding in-house NDT. A machine shop or composite fabricator that has sent parts out for penetrant or UT and now wants the capability in-house needs a written practice, procedures, qualified personnel and records an auditor will accept. We help build the SNT-TC-1A written practice and can explain how a NAS 410-aligned version differs, so you understand what your customer will audit. See written practice development.
  • Audit preparation. Before a customer source inspection or a Nadcap audit, an independent Level III review of training records, experience logs, exam records and vision tests usually finds the gaps faster than an internal check.
  • Outside Level III support. Smaller suppliers often don't have a full-time Level III. We provide Level III oversight for SNT-TC-1A programmes: procedure review, examination administration and technique approval. See our aerospace NDT consulting in Savannah and NDT consulting in Savannah pages, and the statewide NDT consulting in Georgia hub.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical exams are where aerospace candidates most often stumble, usually on set-up and calibration discipline rather than theory. Atlantis's Practical NDT simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods across five virtual environments, including an aircraft hangar. You can rehearse probe handling, scan patterns and indication evaluation as often as you like before a session on real equipment. It's a practice tool only. It doesn't replace the practical examination on real specimens, and no written practice should treat it as one.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, practical sessions and examination administration for the SNT-TC-1A programmes we support.

Frequently asked questions about aerospace NDT training in Savannah

Where can I get aerospace NDT training in Savannah?

Atlantis NDT delivers SNT-TC-1A-based aerospace NDT training for Savannah with live online theory and onsite practicals at your employer's facility. We have no local classroom. If you're employed by a NAS 410 aerospace company, ask its Responsible Level 3 first which outside training the written practice accepts. Ask us about dates and delivery.

Is NAS 410 certification the same as ASNT SNT-TC-1A?

No. Both are employer-based and use similar building blocks: formal training, experience, general, specific and practical exams, and a vision test. NAS 410 is the aerospace standard, with a Responsible Level 3 and stricter controls, and most aerospace primes require it of their suppliers. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice that each employer adapts in its written practice. A certification under one doesn't transfer automatically to the other.

Can I take aerospace NDT training online in Georgia?

The theory, yes. Our live online sessions cover method principles, equipment, technique and specifications. The practical portion and the practical exam need real equipment and specimens, which is why we run them onsite at the employer's facility. Fully online "certification" claims for aerospace NDT should be treated with caution.

Which NDT method should I learn first for aerospace work in Savannah?

Fluorescent penetrant is the classic entry method on production lines. Eddy current is the most valuable second method for MRO hangar work. UT for bonded and composite structure is the method that moves technicians into higher-responsibility roles. Your employer's needs should decide the order. See penetrant testing in aviation and ultrasonic testing in aviation.

How long does aerospace NDT Level II training take?

It depends on the method, your existing certifications and the written practice. Each method and level has its own formal-training and experience minimums, and aerospace employers frequently set more. Rather than quote figures that may not match your employer's document, we point people to the training requirements matrix and then confirm against the written practice.

What does aerospace NDT training cost in Savannah?

We quote on request. Cost depends on the methods and levels, the number of technicians, whether practicals run onsite, and whether you also need written-practice or Level III support. Cohort and onsite quotes go out within one business day. Request a quote.

Do I need a licence to do radiography on aircraft parts in Georgia?

The employer needs the right authorisation. That means a Georgia EPD radioactive materials licence for isotope sources, or Department of Community Health registration for X-ray equipment. The radiographer needs the radiation-safety training and qualification those rules require. These are separate from your NDT method certification.

Will a Savannah aerospace employer accept my ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification?

It won't transfer automatically. A NAS 410 employer will usually review your prior training and experience records and then certify you under its own written practice, including its own examinations. Good records of your SNT-TC-1A training and experience make that bridge much shorter.

Can veterans from Hunter Army Airfield or Air Guard NDI shops move into civilian aerospace NDT?

Yes, and military NDI experience is valued. Military qualifications don't convert directly into civilian certification, though. A civilian employer certifies you under its own written practice, and documented military training and experience can count toward its requirements. A short refresher on civilian specifications and documentation often helps.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for Atlantis training?

Those programmes generally require an approved school, meaning a VA-approved programme for GI Bill benefits or a provider on Georgia's eligible training provider list for WIOA. Atlantis doesn't claim either approval, so check with the VA or your local WorkSource Georgia office. Many Savannah technicians train through employer-paid programmes instead.

Can you train our technicians on our own penetrant line and eddy current equipment?

Yes. That's the core of our onsite model. Practicals run on your equipment and reference standards, using your procedures, so the training matches the work. Ask about onsite training for your Savannah crew.

Do you offer ASNT Level III preparation for aerospace technicians?

Yes. We offer Basic and method examination preparation for experienced Level IIs. See ASNT Level III training and the Level III Basic exam guide. For practice questions at Level II, try the UT Level 2 practice questions.
